title: Gabber criterion fixed-degree vanishing
statement: Under the hypotheses of Gabber criterion, for each fixed positive q, Subsingleton (Sheaf.H F q).

Stacks writes $H^1_{\Et}(D(f),\mathcal F)$ for the cohomology of the object $D(f)$ of $S_{\Et}$, which is $H^1(D(f)_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(f)})$ by Cohomology on Sites Lemma 03F3

proof.text: Induct strongly on n, with the simultaneous claim that H^n of the pullback of F to every D(h) is subsingleton for n>0. For a class xi on D(h), the vanishing-ideal lemma applies using the induction hypotheses for all positive m<n and all principal opens. Obtain an ideal I whose membership is exactly vanishing of the displayed restrictions.

source.place: Lemma 0GY0 (label lemma-gabber-criterion), proof: simultaneous induction on all principal opens, local triviality, and the ideal of vanishing restrictions.

proof.text: For every prime p containing I, assume h is outside p. Local vanishing produces f in I outside p, contradicting I <= p. Thus every prime containing I contains h. Mathlib Ideal.radical_eq_sInf and Submodule.mem_sInf put h in the radical of I. Ideal.mem_radical_iff yields N with h^N in I.

source.place: Lemma 0GY0 (label lemma-gabber-criterion), proof: simultaneous induction on all principal opens, local triviality, and the ideal of vanishing restrictions.

proof.text: The restriction of xi to D(h^N*h) is zero. By pow_succ and PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen_pow, this open equals D(h), even if N=0 or h=0. Scheme.isoOfEq identifies its inclusion with an isomorphism. The existing topological invariance theorem cohomologyMap_bijective makes restriction injective, so xi=0. Any two classes equal zero, proving the simultaneous induction claim.

proof.text: Take h=1. PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen_one and Scheme.topIso identify D(1) with Spec R. Again cohomologyMap_bijective makes the pullback map injective. Its target is subsingleton by the simultaneous induction, hence its source Sheaf.H F q is subsingleton.

split_report.summary: Split Stacks Lemma 0GY0 (etale-cohomology.tex line 14228) into five steps: identify each D(h) with Spec(R_h), identify its local rings with R_p, and apply the 09AX comparison; induct simultaneously over all principal opens D(h), avoiding an unproved localization transport; define I_h as the elements f for which the class vanishes on D(hf), use local Zariski triviality, and show every prime avoiding h avoids I_h; prove closure under addition in degree one by applying the stated kernel hypothesis to hf and hg; and prove higher-degree addition by Mayer-Vietoris, then use h in the radical of I_h to conclude the class vanishes. The proof and source places are recorded directly from the cited Stacks route.
